title: The Verb Agrees With the Thing

sections.title: Same *se*, same agreement
sections.content: You know the passive *se* from B1 Unit 6: *se* plus a verb in the third person says that something is done without saying who does it. The noun after the verb is the subject of the sentence, so the verb agrees with it in number: *Se vende una casa*, but *Se venden casas*. This lesson shows that the agreement holds whenever you have a noun: after two nouns, with the noun in front of the verb, and after *poder* or *deber* plus an infinitive.

sections.title: With poder, deber and an infinitive
sections.content: *Se* goes before the first verb, and that verb agrees with the noun that follows: *Se puede ver el mar*, *Se pueden ver las montañas*. If there is no noun, the verb stays singular: *Se puede entrar*. You know *deber* from B1 Unit 4; it works in the same way.

items.spanish: Se necesitan dos boletos para entrar.
items.english: Two tickets are needed to get in.

sections.content: Two or more nouns joined by *y* usually take a plural verb: *Se venden libros y revistas*. The noun can also come first, and the agreement is the same: *Los acuerdos se firmaron ayer*. In fast speech some people say *Se vendió casas*, but careful Spanish agrees: *Se vendieron casas*.
